evidence: Workbook quality row 51 and its internal annotation require well-formed gating TOML, shell syntax/LF, seed and reference entry; the skill check 51 specifically calls for parser checks. Independently executed Python 3.12.13 tomllib.loads on task.toml, tests/scoring.toml and all five judge.toml files: all seven parsed (criteria counts 1, 1, 86, 14, 6). json.loads accepted both seed copies and package.json. GNU Bash 5.2.26 bash -n returned 0 for solution/solve.sh and tests/test.sh; raw bytes contain no CR and each begins #!/bin/bash followed by LF. node v24.19.0 --check returned 0 for server.js and all six other shipped JS files. ast.parse accepted both shared Python tools without writing bytecode. Frozen server.js:1-2 contains use strict and require(./src/index.js); the dependency exists and parsed. Negative controls rejected malformed TOML, an unfinished shell if, and const x = ; (exit 2 and 1 for shell/JS); valid alternative shell/JS forms parsed. A well-formed entry that requires a missing module could escape syntax-only checks; actual hash-matched Linux lifecycle evidence additionally exercises the real entry and dependencies. local/install-lifecycle.py invokes bash /solution/solve.sh, then a sanitized unprivileged node /app/server.js from /tests; results.json and install-lifecycle-attempt2.log record fresh install exit 0, successful authenticated bootstrap (7 requisitions/13 offers), creation, restart PID 21 to 97, saved-data readback, and closed reinstall. The active-reinstall EACCES is recorded as a refusal and does not represent a fresh-install parser failure. All 11 recorded app hashes matched frozen bytes, plus the indexed solve.sh and environment/seed hashes.
